_comment: Phase 8a. The poller's own give-up state, and the alert
UnknownResolverMetrics was written already expecting: 'every one of these
needs a person... a threshold of more than zero for more than an hour is a
reasonable page' - that sentence is this rule.
WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE RULE FROM unknown-backlog-age, NOT ONE THRESHOLD
UNKNOWN and UNRESOLVED are different questions with different urgency.
UNKNOWN means 'we do not know yet, the poller is working' - a payment can be
in that state for up to ~2h through normal backoff and the age alert next
to this one is tuned around exactly that math. UNRESOLVED means 'we do not
know, and we have stopped asking' - the poller exhausted its 8 attempts and
gave up, so nothing in this system will ever move this payment again without
a person. Folding the two into one rule would mean either paging on normal
backoff or waiting hours to notice a payment nothing is working on anymore;
the phase's own text keeps them as two states for the same reason -
PaymentState.UNRESOLVED's own javadoc: 'one of these is worth waking
somebody up for; a thousand UNKNOWNs at 2am might not be.'
matchType 1, target 0, op > - the same shape as 06-dlq-pending.json and for
the identical reason: there is no healthy non-zero level of a payment
nothing is working on. One is worth a page.
evalWindow 15m rather than the age alert's 5m. UNRESOLVED is set once, by
the poller's own give-up transition (recon/UnknownResolver), not something
that fluctuates - a longer window here only affects how quickly the FIRST
occurrence is noticed, and 15 minutes after a payment has already been
abandoned by automation is not urgency this rule needs to shave finer.
NO alertOnAbsent, same reasoning as unknown-backlog-age.json: this gauge
only exists when the poller is enabled, and most local runs do not enable
it.

annotations.summary: {{$value}} payment(s) the poller has given up on
annotations.description: The automatic UNKNOWN poller exhausted its 8 attempts on at least one payment without a definitive answer from any provider. Nothing in this system will act on it further - it needs a human to look the reference up with each provider directly. See UnknownResolver and payorch.recon.gave_up for how many have accumulated.
